memorial_details:
Name: Avro Lancaster ED549
Type: Stone of remembrance
Description: Granite headstone shaped stone dedicated to the memory of 6 aircrew who died when the aircraft crash landed just to the north of the memorial on the 5 March 1943 after engine trouble following a mine laying operation over France. Flanked by two wooden posts and an information board about the incident.
Inscription: IN MEMORY OF / THE CREW OF / LANCASTER BOMBER ED549 / WHICH CRASHED CLOSE TO / THIS SITE ON RETURNING / FROM OPERATIONS IN FRANCE/ 5TH MARCH 1943 / (Names) / (Name) / WAS THE / SOLE SURVIVOR / WE WILL REMEMBER THEM
Location: Opposite Grange Farm on the Grantham Canal Plungar Melton Leicestershire NG13 0JJ England
Grid Ref: SK 76582 34275
Coordinates: 52.900471341632,-0.862924895393
Photos: https://media.iwm.org.uk/ciim5/memorials/53/854/large_80471.jpg; https://media.iwm.org.uk/ciim5/memorials/173/257/large_80471.jpg; https://media.iwm.org.uk/ciim5/memorials/53/855/large_80471_inscr_lancaster_crash_plungar.jpg

Memorial Unveiling: The unveiling of the Avro Lancaster ED549 memorial.
narrative: On March 5, 1943, Lancaster bomber ED549, belonging to 100 Squadron, tragically crashed near this site upon its return from operations in France. Among the crew, only one individual survived - (Name). This memorial honors the remaining members of the crew who perished that day.
